title: Make an issue board useful
summary: An issue board shows work in columns based on chosen project rules, often using labels. It helps a team see items waiting or in progress.
introduction: An issue board shows work in columns based on chosen project rules, often using labels. It helps a team see items waiting or in progress. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain make an issue board useful
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: An issue board shows work in columns based on chosen project rules, often using labels. It helps a team see items waiting or in progress.

blocks.code:
Board labels: ready, doing, review
Card: Add empty-state text
Current label: doing
Next condition: move to review when the change and checks are ready
blocks.title: Make an issue board useful

blocks.text: The card position communicates a work state. The team needs a clear meaning for each column so movement is useful.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write a rule for when a card may enter ready.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Moving a card does not change the code or prove its checks passed.
For more detail later, use this [GitLab further reading](https://docs.gitlab.com/tutorials/).
